Title: Can large language models provide useful feedback on research papers? A large-scale empirical analysis
Finding: LLM manuscript feedback can be useful, but utility is not equivalent to correct conference compliance.
Limitation: Retrospective review overlap and researcher perceptions do not validate an arbitrary checklist.
Project implication: Use feedback as assistance and validate every criterion on an independently annotated set.

Title: Is LLM a Reliable Reviewer? A Comprehensive Evaluation of LLM on Automatic Paper Reviewing Tasks
Finding: Review generation and score prediction expose limitations in critical and long-document reasoning.
Limitation: Scores and fluent reviews can conceal factual mistakes.
Project implication: Separate formal checks from semantic judgments; permit insufficient_evidence and human review.

Title: Automated Peer Reviewing in Paper SEA: Standardization, Evaluation, and Analysis
Finding: SEA separates standardization, evaluation and consistency analysis in scientific reviewing.
Limitation: Its training and review-generation setting differs from user-supplied conference criteria.
Project implication: Use a staged pipeline and check consistency between a finding and the cited manuscript text.

Title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
Finding: LLM judges approximate some human preferences but have position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases.
Limitation: Chat-assistant preference agreement is not manuscript-compliance accuracy.
Project implication: Evaluate criterion order sensitivity, repeated-run stability and agreement with human labels.

Title: G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment
Finding: Explicit evaluation criteria and structured judging can improve alignment in NLG tasks.
Limitation: Summarization and dialogue findings do not establish validity for scientific paper assessment.
Project implication: Use an explicit rubric and structured outputs; retain a separate human reference.

Title: Prometheus: Inducing Fine-grained Evaluation Capability in Language Models
Finding: Custom rubrics support fine-grained feedback and evaluation.
Limitation: Rubric-conditioned response evaluation and reference answers differ from checking unseen conference rules.
Project implication: Store criterion definitions and rubric versions; benchmark a fixed rubric rather than one global score.

Title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
Finding: Performance can depend on the location of relevant evidence in a long input.
Limitation: The experiments study retrieval tasks, not this project or every future model.
Project implication: Preserve section anchors; test evidence moved to the beginning, middle and end.

Title: Attribute or Abstain: Large Language Models as Long Document Assistants
Finding: Attribution makes long-document responses more verifiable; evidence quality remains task dependent.
Limitation: A citation alone does not guarantee support for a complex claim.
Project implication: Validate quoted spans and ask human annotators whether evidence supports each finding.

Title: Nougat: Neural Optical Understanding for Academic Documents
Finding: Visual document recognition converts academic PDF content into structured markup.
Limitation: A neural parser may introduce recognition errors; reliable formatting checks require retained layout data.
Project implication: Compare layout-aware conversion with plain extraction and explicitly flag unsupported scanned files.

Title: Docling Technical Report
Finding: Layout and table models support structured local PDF conversion.
Limitation: The v1 report does not validate the current package on our PDF/DOCX corpus.
Project implication: Pilot Docling as a parser adapter; measure heading and reading-order accuracy on representative files.

Title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
Finding: Retrieval decisions and critique can improve grounded generation in studied tasks.
Limitation: The trained retrieval-reflection framework is not equivalent to merely adding a vector database.
Project implication: Treat retrieval as an experimental extension; start with explicit section evidence and compare baselines.

Title: Unveiling the Merits and Defects of LLMs in Automatic Review Generation for Scientific Papers
Publication type: Research preprint; reports IEEE ICDM short-paper acceptance
Finding: Structured and descriptive reviews can coexist with weak critical reasoning and contextual grounding.
Limitation: Review-generation benchmarks differ from deterministic and semantic compliance checks.
Project implication: Evaluate correctness, unsupported claims and actionable feedback separately from writing quality.

Title: Official product features
Finding: Configurable journal checks and results linked to marked-up text are publicly documented.
Limitation: Feature claims are vendor descriptions; no hands-on benchmark was performed.
Project implication: Use transparent evidence-linked feedback as an existing-system comparison criterion.

Title: Preflight for Blood Cancer Discovery
Finding: Journal-specific language, technical checks and AI-assisted critique are advertised.
Limitation: This partner configuration does not describe every Paperpal product or arbitrary user-created rubrics.
Project implication: Compare fixed venue workflows with editable conference requirements without claiming universal novelty.

Title: GROBID Introduction
Finding: GROBID restructures scholarly PDF into XML/TEI with metadata, sections and references.
Limitation: It is a parsing component, not a complete compliance evaluator; no project benchmark yet.
Project implication: Include GROBID as a PDF parsing alternative and preserve source provenance.

Title: Structured model outputs
Finding: Structured output can constrain a response to a supported JSON schema.
Limitation: Schema adherence does not establish factual correctness; refusals and failures still need handling.
Project implication: Validate schema, evidence and statuses separately; keep model selection configurable.
